item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W20
item.description: Designed and deployed Unified AI Agent Workflow system across three repositories (gadget, TokenMonitor, LifeCopilot) establishing standardized SPEC→PLAN→IMPLEMENT→VERIFY→REVIEW protocol for cross-agent development. Completed major infrastructure migration moving Miniconda and 4 conda environments from C: to D: drive, freeing ~70 GB. Fixed critical summarize deployment bugs that blocked 72 days of reports from publishing to GitHub Pages.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W18
item.description: Successfully stabilized and released TokenMonitor v0.12.1, resolving 6+ critical Windows platform bugs including hover oscillation feedback loops, tray icon focus issues, window positioning instability, and false positive warnings. Implemented automated Cursor IDE reconnection with token refresh polling, eliminating manual restart requirements. Established robust CI/CD pipeline with comprehensive formatting and linting compliance across multi-platform builds.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W15
item.description: The first two days of this week (W15 opening) focused on two main threads: planning and executing three editorial annotations for the MIHD paper draft, discovering the core new argument of ‘clustering-retrieval tradeoff’ through actual HD immune microenvironment analysis and completing three new cross-section RM-IDEAL benchmark experiments; simultaneously conducting a comprehensive review of website/update.sh, fixing 4 script bugs and helping set up a complete Hugo deployment environment, restoring the website publishing pipeline from continuous failures (exit 1/127/128) to all 7 steps passing.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W14
item.description: This week, three main tasks are being carried out concurrently: preparing the MIHD multimodal spatial transcriptome paper (5 days, DCC), completing the TEDDY full-embedding benchmark, the Leiden comparison experiment, the HD fusion evaluation, and writing the bilingual paper outline; establishing a differentiated research focus on “zero-sample FM embedding fusion”. The TokenMonitor Linux FloatBall systematic fix (5 days) has evolved from symptom correction through multiple iterations to a fixed window + GDK Input Shape architecture reform. All 21 code review issues in PR #4 have also been completed. The Life-Copilot Discord Bot has been fully重构 (2 days), with 2823 lines deleted, a multi-CLI Agent architecture introduced, and multiple new features implemented such as screen time tracking, Feishu input channels, and MCP tool integration. In addition, 63 papers in the NeurIPS 2025 D&B Track have been reviewed, and a new Linux workstation environment has been set up.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W13
item.description: This week’s core work focused on multi-model embedding expansion and issue triage for the MIHD spatial transcriptomics project. On March 23, environment initialization was completed on the DCC HPC cluster, and historical challenges in the MIHD project were systematically documented — for the first time structuring the root cause of cross-section retrieval failure (incomparable embedding spaces) and the single-section ARI gap as formal documents. On March 29, four critical bugs in the TEDDY foundation model extraction script were successfully fixed, the first DLPFC section embedding extraction was completed, and batch runs were launched, establishing the foundation for a multi-model comparison benchmark.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W12
item.description: This week, efforts were made across three devices—DCC, tianhe, and TzJsDesktop—to comprehensively advance two major research directions: robot operation and spatial transcriptomics. The Error Recovery Benchmark achieved progress from design of collection schemes (RBG group with 329 demo budgets) to architectural-level trajectory segmentation reconstruction (InteractionSegmenter), with a total of 1627 training scenes (covering 148 subtypes, +35%); MIHD spatial transcriptomics completed the full pipeline for cross-slide Embedding and established the zero-sample advantage of scGPT (100% accuracy vs UNI2’s 71%); π₀.₅ completed the full training process with loss ≈0.253, and five conditioning strategies (Exp5-9) were designed; the gadget toolchain completed the architectural reconstruction of Research Profiler disambiguation, the construction of a unified deploy staging architecture for the website, and the full upgrade of ECC to opus+max thinking. The key breakthroughs this week focused on “identifying and resolving architectural root causes”: the non-comparable per-section PCA coordinate system, ambiguity in multi-object target_object, and Flax NNX inheritance vs combination—these three systematic issues were fundamentally resolved this week.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W11
item.description: This week, six main projects were advanced in parallel on three devices: DCC, tianhe, and TzJsDesktop. ① The fundamental flaw in the MIHD spatial transcriptomics discovery cross-sample embedding methodology was identified (independent processing per section leads to non-comparable feature spaces), and remediation efforts were initiated. ② The ErrorRecoveryBenchmark has been scaled up comprehensively from bug fixes to 13 skills/29 sub-types, overcoming the problem of dropped skill objects not falling down. After revealing the limitations of the online quota architecture, a new offline injection direction was established. ③ VLA-RoboTwin/pi05 has completed the entire workflow from environment setup and training performance optimization (JAX version alignment + 33% speedup) to data variable collection and auxiliary task experiments. ④ The gadget toolchain has undergone an architectural upgrade with MCP Server + common/shared packages + a unified output directory, and the research profiler has exceeded the student discovery priority on scholar profiles. ⑤ CalendarPro has been fully optimized across 7 stages, passing all 230 tests, and token consumption has been reduced by 40–60%. ⑥ The gadget research toolchain has integrated citation graph analysis and completed in-depth profiles of 7 embodied AI scholars.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W10
item.description: This week, across three devices—DCC, Tianhe Supercomputing, and TzJsDesktop—four main projects were advanced in parallel: space transcriptome research, robot operation training/assessment, AI personal assistant, and paper management tools. The MIHD project completed the full set of fusion experiments for scGPT+UNI2 (QFormer avg ARI=0.370, +117% vs scGPT-only) and established a zero-shot cross-sample assessment framework; Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning achieved a total success rate of 58.9%, fully surpassing BC-RNN (0%), thereby quantitatively validating the advantages of the VLA model; CalendarPro achieved a structural leap from passive response to active decision-making (321 tests all passed), while exposing and fixing critical integration defects such as the BackgroundCoordinator never starting; gadget Research Scout was built from scratch to production-ready, completing a two-stage LLM paper evaluation pipeline in a single day and providing three research direction suggestions for the first time; error_recovery_benchmark completed the full cleanup of 65 symlinks and the infrastructure for visualizing error scenarios in MP4 format. The most important engineering experience this week is: test passing ≠ system availability (the integration layer must be verified independently), and before designing an agentic system, it is necessary to actively study the architectural patterns of mature similar projects.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W09
item.description: This week, two main tracks—space transcriptomics (MIHD) and robot error recovery benchmark—were advanced in parallel on both DCC and Tianhe clusters. On DCC, the bug related to fatal weight loading in scGPT was fixed (average ARI improvement of 44.4%), the MIHD benchmark was extended to the Visium HD dataset, and a large-scale repository refactoring of approximately 250K lines of code was completed; on Tianhe, the BC-RNN Phoenix baseline training pipeline was established from scratch (9 tasks run in parallel), the root cause of the 0% success rate in the Pi0.5 evaluation was identified and fixed, key conclusions were obtained for the M14 baseline evaluation (the learning strategy achieves SR≈0 in error scenarios, proving the necessity of M15 LoRA fine-tuning), and the Pi0.5 LoRA 9 task was successfully fine-tuned in parallel on 6×A800 with stable operation.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W08
item.description: This week, with the MIHD spatial transcriptomics project as the main focus, a systematic investigation was completed on H&E Image-Only clustering (establishing a literature baseline of ARI 0.11–0.16), three self-supervised enhancement methods were implemented (SCAN increased ARI from 0.251 to 0.303, +20.6%), and a two-stage fusion framework for Vision Refinement was established; meanwhile, on the tianhe cluster, the Error Recovery Benchmark (M14 evaluation infrastructure verification, full assessment of 649 scenarios started) and the Phoenix pi0.5 reproduction data pipeline (18.4GB MimicGen dataset stored, training configuration in place) were advanced in parallel. Throughout the week, multiple engineering bottlenecks such as STEGO NaN, double normalization bug, lerobot version conflicts, and HuggingFace proxy issues were resolved. The two bottlenecks related to Pi0.5 OOM and visualize_scene.py video validation will be postponed to next week.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W07
item.description: This week, progress was made across three areas: robot simulation, bioinformatics, and toolchains. error_recovery_benchmark encountered a deep bottleneck in force injection debugging (30N has no visible effect on the OSC controller), revealing fundamental issues with the controller compensation mechanism; MIHD completed the Chinese documentation for the enhancement plan; ccusage implemented billing support for multiple GLM models and passed type/form checking; robobrain_pi confirmed that the training pipeline is ready. This week, AI revealed obvious pattern-matching flaws in repeated errors (SSH missing “cd” command) and environmental assumptions (proxy, pnpm), while humans provided more efficient debugging approaches at key decision points (extreme force testing, detecting local GPU, reusing existing pricing files).

item.title: Weekly Summary 2026-W06
item.description: This week (2026-02-06~07), the work focused on two main areas: first, a systematic root-cause analysis was conducted on the ARI performance gap between staig_fusion in the MIHD project and the original STAIG (0.21→target 0.56), and five key implementation differences were identified and quantified. The code layer work related to strict alignment coverage improvement was also completed; second, the benchmark tool was upgraded for engineering use, including fixing the bar chart rendering bug in the report, and implementing an end-to-end GitHub Pages automatic publishing pipeline as well as a CLI interaction upload function. In addition, an English TOEFL speaking practice session (personal study) was recorded.

item.title: Weekly Summary 2025-W40
item.description: In this week (2025-W40), there is only one valid session record on October 2nd, and that session remained in the initialization stage. After opening the core tracking and segmentation files of the AutoSeg-SAM2 project, the user did not engage in any substantive development work. Overall, there was no significant progress this week.
